subject: general
question: Who was the last ruler of Nanda dynasty?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhana Nanda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dhana Nanda** was the **last ruler** of the **Nanda Dynasty**, which held power over the **Magadha** region in ancient India during the **4th century BCE**.
 
• He was the youngest of the **nine sons** of **Mahapadma Nanda**, who are collectively known in historical and religious texts as the **Navanandas**.
 
• During his reign, **Alexander the Great** invaded the north-western part of India in **326 BCE**. Historical accounts suggest that Alexander's army refused to cross the **Beas River** primarily due to the fear of **Dhana Nanda's** massive and formidable military force.
 
• His rule came to an end around **322–321 BCE** when he was defeated and **overthrown** by **Chandragupta Maurya**, who was assisted by the strategic brilliance of **Chanakya** (Kautilya).
 
• The downfall of **Dhana Nanda** marked the transition from the Nanda period to the **Mauryan Empire**, which eventually unified most of the Indian subcontinent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mahapadma Nanda**:

 
 
• He was the **founder** of the Nanda dynasty and is often regarded as the first **historical emperor** of India.
 
• In the **Puranas**, he is described as **"Sarva-Kshatrantaka"** (the uprooter of all Kshatriyas) and **"Ekarat"** (the sole monarch).
 
• He successfully expanded the **Magadhan Empire** by conquering various kingdoms like the **Kurus**, **Panchalas**, and **Kashis**.
 
 
 
• **The Nanda Military**:
 
 
• The dynasty was famous for its **military strength**. According to Greek historians like **Curtius**, the Nanda army consisted of **200,000 infantry**, **20,000 cavalry**, **2,000 chariots**, and **3,000 elephants**.
 
• This immense power ensured that **Magadha** remained the most dominant **Mahajanapada** of its time.
 
 
 
• **Economic and Social Conditions**:
 
 
• The name **"Dhana"** implies **wealth**. Ancient texts mention that the Nandas had accumulated **vast treasures** through a highly organized system of **taxation**.
 
• However, **Dhana Nanda** became highly **unpopular** among his subjects due to his **oppressive** tax regimes and his low-born status, which was looked down upon by the contemporary social elite.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Navanandas (The Nine Nandas)**:

 
 
• According to **Buddhist traditions** found in the **Mahabodhivamsa**, the nine kings were **Ugrasena** (Mahapadma Nanda), **Panduka**, **Pandugati**, **Bhuta-pala**, **Rashtra-pala**, **Govishanaka**, **Dashasiddhaka**, **Kaivarta**, and **Dhana Nanda**.
 
• They ruled for a relatively short duration, approximately **22 to 28 years**, but left a lasting impact on Indian administration.
 
 
 
• **Capital**:
 
 
• The **capital** of the Nanda Empire was **Pataliputra** (modern-day **Patna**). It was a major center for **trade**, **politics**, and **education**.
 
 
 
• **Role of Chanakya**:
 
 
• The friction between **Chanakya** and **Dhana Nanda** is a significant historical theme. After being **insulted** in the Nanda court, Chanakya swore to destroy the dynasty and trained **Chandragupta Maurya** to fulfill this objective.
